ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the mass spectrum of zirconium, with the horizontal axis labeled Atomic mass and the vertical axis labeled Relative abundance (%). There are several labeled peaks in the figure: Zr-90, Zr-91, Zr-92, Zr-94, and Zr-96. Among them, the bar peak of Zr-90 is the highest, with an abundance of about more than 50%, so the most common isotope is zirconium-90. Reasoning: The question asks how many neutrons the most common isotope of zirconium has. The atomic number of zirconium is 40, indicating that each zirconium atom has 40 protons. The mass number of Zr-90 is 90, so the number of neutrons = mass number - number of protons = 90 - 40 = 50.
